title: Define cross-team acceptance gates for model quantization rollout and regression-eval criteria
creator: Aisha Ramesh
description:
Background: The PRD proposes introducing an optional 4-bit quantized model variant for hosted and dedicated deployments to reduce per-token cost and improve throughput for long-sequence workloads. This ticket establishes the cross-functional acceptance gates (Engineering, Design, Legal/Compliance, Product) required before enabling the quantized variant in any production rollout.

Scope: Define clear, testable acceptance criteria for functional parity, quality regressions, latency/cost thresholds, telemetry and rollback triggers. Produce a checklist and owner matrix for: model onboarding, kernel/serving runtime validation, client SDK compatibility, console feature flags, documentation, and legal review for any model licensing/redistribution constraints.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before canary release):
- Quality: No more than 0.5% regression on weighted NLG evals across our priority prompt set (prompt-set: quant-opt-2026-v1). Any regression must have a documented mitigation (prompt tweaks, fallback path).
- Safety: No new high-severity safety regressions identified by automated evals or red-team tests.
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency for write workloads must improve or be within 10% of baseline for <2s completion targets.
- Cost: Expected per-token serving cost estimate demonstrates >=25% unit cost reduction at target throughput given batching and KV-cache behavior.
- Telemetry: New metrics (quant_variant_enabled, quant_fallback_rate, quant_quality_score) are instrumented and visible in Console per-route dashboards with 90-day retention for early rollout.
- Rollback: Automated fallback to FP16/FP32 must occur within 2 minutes for any route with fallback_rate > 3% or error rate > 1% for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Legal/License: Legal confirms redistribution and deployment of the quantized model variant is permitted for hosted and dedicated customers, or documents contractual constraints and required customer notices.

Deliverables: PRD appendix enumerating eval datasets and scoring scripts (link), runbook for canary -> ramp -> GA, Console feature-flag design, SDK compatibility notes, and a verification checklist to be signed by ENG, Design, and Legal approvers.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include implementing the quantization kernels in the runtime (ENG will deliver), nor the billing integration for per-variant pricing (separate PM ticket).

Owner matrix: Product: Aisha Ramesh (overall), Engineering: Marco Chen (validation & runtime signoff), Design: Sofia Alvarez (console UX & customer messaging), Legal: Priya Kapoor (license/compliance signoff).

Links: PRD (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRD/quantization-rollout-2026, Eval dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/quant-opt-2026, Draft runbook (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/quant-runbook-2026

What is the acceptable SLA delta for customers on Dedicated vs Hosted when using quantized variants?
Do we require an explicit customer-facing changelog entry for GA or only console-level notices?
